Before we begin, I want all of us to remember Mr. Ashok Bhandari, our Special Advisor, he 
passed away suddenly 2 days after our Q1 results call. Many of you know him from these calls. 
He earned the trust of the investor community. During his tenure, the market cap of Shree

him. We will miss him. We miss him every time. Our condolences are with his family. May his 
soul rest in peace. 
 
Going into our quarterly performance. The second quarter is usually a softer quarter for the 
cement industry. This year, it was also affected by the conflict in West Asia and by a weak 
monsoon in most regions. East was an exception. Against this backdrop, our focus on volumes 
continued to deliver results. India sales volumes increased by approximately 18% year-on-year 
from 7.91 million tons to 9.31 million tons. 
 
Realizations improved marginally by 1% from INR4,840 per ton to INR4,870 per ton. Consol 
EBITDA rose by about 4% from INR974 crores to INR1,016 crores. However, consolidated 
EBITDA per ton declined to INR966 from INR1,055 a year ago, primarily due to a higher fuel 
cost.

Consol sales volumes also grew by about 14% from 9.23 million tons to 10.52 million tonnes. 
This improvement in volumes was also supported by better capacity utilization in our India 
operations, which increased to 56% compared to 52% in the corresponding quarter last year. 
 
On a sequential basis, against the first quarter, the numbers are lower, which is what the season 
usually brings. India volume fell 11% from 10.49 million tons to 9.31 million tonnes. Realization 
was 1% lower at INR4,870 against INR4,919.  
Consol EBITDA declined from INR1,272 crores to INR1,016 crores, while EBITDA per ton 
moved to INR966 from INR1,111. Consol sales volumes were down by 8% from 11.45 million 
tons to 10.52 million tons. 
 
Our capacity expansion program continues to progress. In September '26, Union Cement 
Company, our step-down subsidiary in the United Arab Emirates, commissioned a new cement 
mill with an annual capacity of 3 million tonnes. This takes its total cement production capacity 
to 7 million tons per annum. 
 
In India, work is progressing on our greenfield integrated plant in Meghalaya, which is expected 
to be commissioned in the quarter ending 31st March 2028. We continue to evaluate and pursue 
strategic expansion opportunities across our markets with a focus on building capacity and 
delivering our long-term growth objectives. 
 
A few words on ready-mix concrete business. Our ready-mix concrete business continues to 
grow and has continued to grow in the last quarter also. The commercial network is now 28 
plants with captive units, the total is 35 plants. The plants which have been running longer, did 
quite well, and the new ones are ramping up. 
 
Volume rose 153% year-on-year to 2.73 lakh cubic meter. Revenue rose 182% to INR129 crores. 
The business stayed EBITDA positive. As each plant fills up, its fixed cost is spread over more 
cubic meters, and that shows in the numbers. We have said for some years that ready-mix is 
where cement in India is heading. This quarter is a small step in that direction. 
 
As you all know, sustainability remains an integral part of our operating strategy. In Q2 FY27, 
green electricity accounted for 65.2% of total electricity consumption, including our wholly 
owned subsidiaries in India. I believe these are amongst one of the highest levels in the Indian 
cement industry, if not the global cement industry. 
 
Our green power generation capacity currently stands at 667 megawatts, including our wholly 
owned subsidiary in India, and we are progressing additional projects to further increase the 
share of green power in our energy mix. For us, saving energy and saving cost are the same 
work. Every unit of green power we add makes per ton cleaner and not only cheaper to produce. 
 
All our manufacturing locations operate on a zero liquid discharge basis, treating, recycling and 
reusing 100% of the wastewater generated by our operations. These initiatives helped us to 
achieve a water quality index of more than 8x in FY26. We remain committed to sustaining and 
improving this performance in the current financial year.

only in the quality of our product, but also in how we serve our customers, invest for the future

urbanization and stable macroeconomic conditions are all helping. A weak monsoon may hold 
back rural demand for some time, but spending on road, railways, housing and data center 
continues, and that will keep India cement demand moving in a positive direction.
